subject.title: Crestodian chat hijacks natural language into operations; approvals require a literal hardcoded yes

question: Should normal Crestodian chat become strictly AI-first while deterministic parsing remains only for exact typed commands, rescue, and no-model fallback?
rationale: The source supports real bugs, but the final boundary changes setup UX, approval intent, rescue behavior, and security-sensitive mutation handling, so maintainer intent should set the contract before landing a broad fix.

options.title: Adopt AI-first boundary
options.body: Make natural language route through the agent/planner, keep deterministic parsing anchored, and repair approval, stale proposal, redaction, rescue, and Gemini parity together.

options.title: Ship safety subset first
options.body: Anchor dangerous regexes and improve literal approval handling first while leaving directives, executor refactor, and Gemini parity for separate review.

options.title: Split the umbrella
options.body: Keep this issue canonical but require smaller follow-ups for parser safety, approval intent, stale state, sensitive history, executor refactor, and Gemini parity.

recommendation.title: Adopt AI-first boundary
recommendation.body: Make natural language route through the agent/planner, keep deterministic parsing anchored, and repair approval, stale proposal, redaction, rescue, and Gemini parity together.

likelyOwner.reason: The merged Crestodian feature history and the linked candidate PR both point to steipete as the product and security-boundary owner for this area.
